voice.v: Institutional but warm, first-person plural: "we", "our alliance".
Questions or promises of 3 to 8 words. Sentence case.
Short imperatives ending in "!": Apply now! Register now! Subscribe now!
Medium weight inside light text. No italics, no underlines, no emoji.
Comma thousands with "+" for totals: +368,000 students.

tlSteps.t: Check if it is worth communicating
tlSteps.d: Identify if you have a relevant outcome. Does it involve a result, a deliverable, an open call, an event, or a milestone that matters to an audience outside your direct team?

Keep your local team informed. If your action is described in the Description of the Action (DoA) and requires involvement from WP8, contact the relevant person directly and the Secretariat, always keeping your institution's Communication Manager in CC.
Do this as early as possible. Outline your communication needs using the provided Briefing Template. Your Communication Manager will review it and confirm the final timeline and channels.
Gather the essential that could help design a good communication strategy. Two-line key message, facts and figures, contact person, links, and images with usage rights.
Emblem, "Co-funded by the European Union", OpenEU logo and, where required, the disclaimer.
Regularly share key highlights and updates for alliance-wide amplification and inclusion in the central OpenEU newsletter.

cmSteps.d: Monitor initiatives led by your university. Evaluate communication requirements and determine ownership. If necessary, refer requests to the appropriate person or institution.
Outline the core elements: Work Packages involved, target audiences, channels, narratives, and KPIs. You can use the provided Briefing Template.
Tailor any communication you generate or receive to your local language, cultural context, and preferred channels.

Every communication effort should aim to expand the OpenEU community. Always include in all supports (forms, website, workshops, eg) Calls to Action (CTAs)  directing audiences to subscribe to the newsletter, and follow OpenEU social channels.
Ensure compliance: no materials can be published without the mandatory EU visibility elements and logos.
Regularly share key highlights and updates from your university for alliance-wide amplification and inclusion in the central OpenEU newsletter.

statements.label: Purpose
statements.text: To create the first pan-European Open University, making quality higher education accessible to anyone, anywhere, at any time.

statements.label: Mission
statements.text: Establish a learner-centred, inclusive, digital and green open university with a European scope, which empowers individuals to lead their own skills' development for enhancing their employability and widens access to quality higher education and lifelong learning (*Leaving no one behind).

statements.label: Vision
statements.text: To become the pan-European Open University that harnesses digital education for - and with - lifelong learners and communities to make a better world.

statements.label: Positioning
statements.text: To be perceived as the undisputed European reference in digital, inclusive and open education, and a catalyst for the transformation of higher education.

routeOptions.title: Partner-Led Initiative (Local leadership)
routeOptions.text: The initiative is led by a single alliance member. This applies to university-led sub-tasks, or actions localized to a campus, or initiatives that rely primarily on local resources.
routeOptions.rule: This request must be routed to and executed by your local University's Decentralised Communications Office. The Central Unit will provide only secondary amplification once assets are fully ready.

routeOptions.title: Joint Alliance-Wide Initiative
routeOptions.text: The initiative directly impacts all 10 partners simultaneously (e.g., joint degree programme, alliance-wide governance, global branding, EU institutional reporting).
routeOptions.rule: This request will be co-managed between the Local Office and the central unit. The Central-unit will help to cross-coordinate assets with all 10 partner hubs.

routeOptions.title: Task linked to cooperation with WP8
routeOptions.text: This proposal is included in the DoA or in the agreements that require the direct intervention of a sub-task defined in the WP8 list.
routeOptions.example: Tadt Podcast (UAb) | Conference Eadtu (OUNL) | Wider campaign (OUC)
routeOptions.rule: If in this request the WP8 task required has not received the information, the central unit will be responsible for forwarding the request to the corresponding WP8 task leader.

challenges.title: Digital transformation of higher education
challenges.text: Our know-how in digital technologies for learning and teaching, research and innovation, engagement, governance and management puts OpenEU in an ideal position to lead the digital transformation of higher education, scaling up cooperation and knowledge exchange that foster internationalisation and personalisation.

challenges.title: Inclusive and equitable higher education
challenges.text: Our long-standing focus on non-traditional students and underrepresented groups lets OpenEU widen access and participation in higher education and help protect and promote European democratic values.

challenges.title: Lifelong learning
challenges.text: Our experience in online and flexible education commits OpenEU to making lifelong learning a reality, using technology to provide the knowledge and skills needed to meet today’s social, economic and environmental challenges.

keyArguments.title: Expanded access to higher education
keyArguments.text: Many learners depend on flexible and accessible modalities, so recognising them fully is essential for fair, equitable and inclusive mobility.

keyArguments.title: Social equity through open education
keyArguments.text: Today’s learners are mostly adults, workers and non-traditional online students, which shows the limits of mandatory physical mobility.
keyArguments.proof: 84% work while they study · 36 years old on average

keyArguments.title: Lifelong learning opportunities
keyArguments.text: Digital and hybrid learning underpin Europe’s skills, reskilling and upskilling agenda and respond to the growing demand for flexible pathways at every stage of life.
keyArguments.proof: Aligned with the Education 2030 agenda and the digital economy
